title: Small brown planthopper infestation enhances it reproduction and insecticide tolerance by manipulating glucose distribution and levels in rice
abstract: The evolutionary arms race between plants and insects involves not only direct defense and counter-defense but also sophisticated resource manipulation. However, how herbivorous insects respond to host nutritional signals to modulate their fitness traits remains unclear. This study investigates how the small brown planthopper (SBPH, Laodelphax striatellus) manipulates host plant carbohydrate allocation, and to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which the acquired glucose enhances SBPH fecundity and insecticide tolerance. Using molecular, pharmacological, and biochemical approaches, we found that SBPH infestation induced systemic carbohydrate reallocation in rice, elevating whole-plant glucose levels by promoting aerial accumulation while depleting root reserves. abstract: Nutrient resorption is a key plant strategy for nutrient conservation, yet whether it responds plastically to non-nutrient stressors such as salinity remains unresolved. title: Open source laser-scanning photostimulation for neuroscience with Zapit
abstract: Optogenetic tools are indispensable for understanding the causal neural mechanisms underlying animal behavior, providing millisecond-precision control over genetically defined neural populations. Random-access laser-scanning optogenetics is a powerful and underutilized method for transiently manipulating cortical activity in mice. Despite the utility of this technique, no general-purpose open-source implementation currently exists, and potential users need expertise across optics, real-time hardware control, and programming. This represents a major barrier to adoption, particularly for newly established research groups. Here we present ‘Zapit’, the first open-source general-purpose platform for random-access laser-scanning optogenetic experiments in head-fixed mice. title: Mid-zone hepatocytes trade proliferation for survival via Atf4-Chop axis in early acute liver injury
abstract: Hepatocytes undergo extensive proliferation to facilitate liver repair after injury, yet early adaptive changes prior to proliferation remain unclear. Using a mouse model of acetaminophen (APAP)-induced liver injury, we show that hepatocytes undergo transient proliferation suppression that is most pronounced in mid-zone hepatocytes, consistent with zonal APAP metabolism. Although spatial transcriptomics (ST) alone could not independently confirm zonal proliferative restraint, ST analysis identified a unique mid-zone stress-response program centered on the Atf4-Chop axis. By integrating Cut&Run with immunohistochemistry and functional studies, we found that the Atf4-Chop axis suppresses proliferation via the cell-cycle inhibitor Btg2. Together, our findings support a model in which mid-zone hepatocytes transiently prioritize stress adaptation over proliferation, thereby preserving regenerative capacity for subsequent liver repair.

title: Heterogeneous responses to embryonic critical period perturbations within the Drosophila larval locomotor circuit
abstract: As developing neural circuits become functional, they undergo a phase of heightened plasticity that facilitates network tuning in response to intrinsic and/or extrinsic stimuli. These developmental windows are termed critical periods (CPs) because perturbations during but not outside the CP can lead to lasting changes, such as the formation of sub-optimal or unstable networks. How separate but connected elements within a network might respond differently to a CP perturbation is not well understood. To study this, we used the locomotor network of the Drosophila larva as a model and heat stress as a CP stimulus that has ecological relevance. abstract: Visualizing the structures of small proteins and complexes has been a longstanding challenge in single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). Some of these targets have been successfully resolved by binding to antibody fragments (Fabs) or fusing with external scaffolds to increase their size. Recent advances in conventional single-particle techniques have enabled the determination of an increasing number of structures smaller than 100 kDa, achieving resolutions relevant to drug research. title: The new paradox of women’s health research
abstract: Women have long been underrepresented in biomedical research, prompting efforts to make research more sex inclusive. These advances are essential, but they can create an unintended tension when rigorous inclusion is interpreted as requiring extensive hormonal or reproductive characterization, even when such detail is unnecessary for the question being asked. We examine this paradox, in which standards intended to strengthen research on women may inadvertently make some studies involving females harder to pursue. We argue that characterization should match the claim a study is designed to support, and that funders, institutions and journals must provide the resources needed to make such rigor feasible. Methodological progress should ultimately broaden, not narrow, the evidence base needed to improve women’s health.

title: Morphology and ultrastructure of pharyngeal sense organs of Drosophila larvae
abstract: This study provides a comprehensive ultrastructural analysis of the pharyngeal sensory system in Drosophila melanogaster larvae, focusing on the four major pharyngeal sense organs: the ventral pharyngeal sensilla (VPS), dorsal pharyngeal sensilla (DPS), dorsal pharyngeal organ (DPO), and posterior pharyngeal sensilla (PPS). Our analysis revealed 15 sensilla across these organs, comprising four mechanosensory, nine chemosensory, and two dual-function sensilla. We identified 35 Type I neurons (6 mechanosensory and 29 chemosensory) and 6 Type II neurons with putative chemosensory functions. Additional sensory structures, including papilla sensilla and chordotonal organs in the cephalopharyngeal region, were characterized. abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) causes more deaths annually than any other pathogen, yet an effective vaccine remains elusive. IFN-γ-producing Th1 CD4+ T cells are necessary but insufficient for protection against infection. In humans, the development of IL-17A-producing Th17 T cells correlates with protection; however, not all individuals develop a Th17 response. In mice, experimental vaccines can elicit protective Th17 cells, yet Th17s are rare in primary infection. Why Mtb fails to consistently elicit Th17s is unknown. Next, using Tbx21-deficient mice, we show that Mtb drives a Th1 response that is only partially protective and limits Th17 cell production in an IFN-γ-independent manner. abstract: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? abstract: Interleukin-21 receptor engagement initiates a Janus kinase–signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) signalling cascade that activates several STAT proteins that drive the germinal centre (GC) response. title: Mapping the topographic organization of the human zona incerta using diffusion MRI
abstract: The zona incerta (ZI) is a deep brain region originally described by Auguste Forel as an ‘immensely confusing area about which nothing can be said’. Despite the elusive nature of this structure, mounting evidence supports the role of the ZI and surrounding regions across a diverse range of brain functions and as a candidate target for neuromodulatory therapies. title: Olfactory combinatorial coding supports risk–reward decision-making in Caenorhabditis elegans
abstract: Olfactory-driven behaviors are essential for animal survival, but mechanisms for decoding olfactory inputs remain poorly understood. abstract: During locomotion, the coordinated activity of dozens of muscles shapes the kinematic features of each stride, including systematic changes in limb movement across walking speed. abstract: Ongoing experience is continuously processed in the context of past events. Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11152-9

A multi-tissue signalling system links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans.

title: WEE1 opposes APC/C<sup>CDH1</sup> activity to promote S phase entry
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11188-x

Experimental and modelling data indicate that WEE1 promotes re-entry of quiescent cells into the cell cycle, potentially explaining the toxic side effects of WEE1 inhibitors in cancer therapies.

title: A single archaeon couples long-chain fatty acid oxidation to methanogenesis
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11207-x

Methanoglobus dolicholipophagus AA-75 is a thermophilic archaeon isolated from a Chinese petroleum reservoir that converts methanol into methane, carbon dioxide and acetate, and uses saturated and unsaturated fatty acids to produce methane.

title: An environmentally regulated dichotomy in cell lineages of the root
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11179-y

An environment-regulated state is identified across multiple cell types at the root tip, revealing a shared dichotomy between cells with and without this state.

title: CD51 delineates functionally distinct astrocyte subtypes in neural circuits
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11186-z

CD51+ astrocytes promote synapse formation in the developing cortex, circuit plasticity in the hippocampus and circuit remodelling after stroke.

title: Persistent neuronal stress signalling underlies Angelman syndrome phenotypes
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11165-4

Genetic and proteomic analyses in human neurons and mouse models of Angelman syndrome (AS) show that loss of the ubiquitin ligase UBE3A leads to an overabundance of asparagine synthetase, and that this is linked with many AS phenotypes.

title: Structural basis for protocadherin-1 recognition by New World hantaviruses
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11184-1

The structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike defines the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition.

title: GRP75-dependent SIMPA mediates inter-organellar quality control
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10733-y

Proteotoxic stress drives formation of GRP75-dependent protein aggregates that signal through mitochondria–ER contact sites to activate targeted quality-control pathways, enabling selective clearance of damaged proteins and preserving mitochondrial integrity.

title: Programmable design of functional proteins from natural language
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11205-z

Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter artificial intelligence model, designs functional proteins from natural-language descriptions, demonstrating experimentally validated activities and improved CO2-fixation product yields without iterative optimization.

title: Octupole-driven spin torque switching of antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11172-5

All-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions can display both a large TMR and a reciprocal switching effect, octupole-driven spin-transfer torque, enabling nanoscale magnetic memory and potentially room-temperature terahertz spintronic devices.

title: Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11168-1

Fifteen years of atmospheric CO2 measurements show that the Amazon carbon sink is weakening, with fires, deforestation and climate stress driving increasingly high carbon emissions.

title: The proteome of Middle Pleistocene Xujiayao and common Denisovan morphology
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11132-z

Denisovans from the Xujiayao and other East Asian sites are morphologically distinctive, with a low cranial profile with near-parallel lateral walls, a massive supraorbital torus, a flat zygomaxillary region and weak prognathism.

title: Functional architecture of the human insula
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11175-2

A functional architecture of the human insula links cytoarchitecture to directed and asymmetric electrophysiological interactions, with mechanistic implications for cognitive modulation of pain and interoceptive experience.

title: Touch-sensing digital pixel fibre enables interactive garment GUI
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11128-9

Multifunctional digital fibres integrate display, touch sensing, computation and multimodal input–output, enabling flexible, washable garments with interactive graphical interfaces and wireless multimedia capabilities.

title: Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11194-z

Climate-driven drought and prey decline triggered lynx predation on raptors, reducing raptor fitness and abundance and producing cascading effects across lower trophic levels.

title: Additive manufacturing of ultralong and architected single crystals
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11185-0

A free-form additive manufacturing method that uses alternating and pulsed heat inputs is described for fabricating metre-tall, centimetre-diameter single crystals of Ti-6Al-4V, as well as hard-to-process refractory metals, including W, Mo, Nb and MoNb alloys.

title: Enzyme-embedded polyesters for accelerated biodegradation in the deep sea
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11192-1

Near-complete deep-sea degradation of enzyme-embedded compostable polyesters shows that thermal enzyme embedding greatly accelerates breakdown across marine environments while preserving material performance, offering a promising strategy to mitigate persistent ocean plastic pollution.

title: The anatomy of a personal health agent
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11161-8

A multi-agent framework that coordinates data science, medical reasoning and health coaching over longitudinal wearable and clinical data to provide holistic personal health support is described.
